title: Devon Conway Ruled Out of India ODI Series With Concussion; Nick Kelly Called In
excerpt: Conway and Matt Henry collided at fielding practice before the Auckland opener. Henry has been cleared for Saturday's second ODI in Wellington; Conway will miss the remaining four matches.
body:
• New Zealand batter Devon Conway has been ruled out of the entire ODI series against India with a concussion suffered in a training collision with Matt Henry.
  • Henry has been cleared of concussion and is available for selection for the second ODI in Wellington on Saturday.
  • Nick Kelly, originally picked only for the fourth and fifth ODIs, joins the squad in Wellington; Dale Phillips replaces him in the New Zealand A squad.
  • India won the series opener in Auckland and lead the five-match series 1-0.

A concussion has ruled New Zealand batter Devon Conway out of the ODI series against India. Conway and fast bowler Matt Henry collided during fielding practice on the eve of the series opener in Auckland and both missed Wednesday's first match, ESPNcricinfo reported. The outcomes have since split: Conway will play no part in the remainder of the series, while Henry has been cleared of concussion and is available for the second ODI in Wellington on Saturday.

The replacement

Nick Kelly, who was originally selected for only the fourth and fifth ODIs, now joins the New Zealand squad in Wellington. Kelly has been withdrawn from the New Zealand A squad, which begins the third match of its unofficial Test series against India A in Lincoln on Saturday, with his place in that side going to Auckland batter Dale Phillips. Cricket Times reported the same squad moves, and noted Henry Nicholls had already been added to the senior ODI squad last week.

What it changes

New Zealand lose their first-choice opener for four remaining matches against an India side that won the Auckland opener — India Today reporting cited in series coverage put the first-match result as an India win by five wickets. Conway's absence pushes Kelly, a left-handed top-order batter, into contention a week earlier than planned, and leaves New Zealand's top order reshuffled for the Wellington match. Conway's recovery target, per series reporting, is the two-match Test series against India that begins in Wellington on November 19 — a timeline that underlines why New Zealand Cricket took no risk with the remaining ODIs.

For India, the equation is simpler: a 1-0 lead, a settled side, and an opponent missing a senior batter. The second ODI is in Wellington on Saturday, November 7.
